counterexample: For iid Uniform[-1/2,1/2] and H the normalized 4x4 Hadamard matrix, take A=H^T diag(1,2,-3,4) H. For every choice of one spectral coordinate k as Q_rest=lambda_k Y_k^2 and the other three as Q3, conditioning at Q_rest=lambda_k(1-epsilon)^2 confines all three core coordinates to magnitude <=epsilon. Hence the conditional Q3 law is supported on an interval of length <=18 epsilon^2 and has density cap at least 1/(18 epsilon^2), so sup_b ||p_(Q3|Q_rest=b)||_infinity=infinity. Distinct eigenvalues remove basis-choice ambiguity.
same_instance_positive_bound: For the displayed A, the physical principal block on (X1,X2) is [[1,1/2],[1/2,1]] with determinant 3/4. Conditioning on (X3,X4) and bounding the cap-one product law by ellipse-shell area gives ||p_Q||_infinity <= 2*pi/sqrt(3) for every admissible independent coordinate law. Thus only the scalar-conditioning supremum gate fails.
replacement_obligation: Test the weighted mixture norm integral ||p_(Q3|Q_rest=b)||_infinity dmu_Qrest(b), or a weaker Lorentz/product-rearrangement surrogate, instead of the false uniform conditional supremum.
